summary: Adds an IMAP extension that lets a client ask the server for a short text preview of a message. Mail apps can show this snippet in the message list without downloading the whole message.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8970 lets an IMAP server provide a short text preview of each message, so email clients can show a snippet without downloading the whole message.

subtitle: Lets an IMAP mail client ask the server for a short, ready-made text preview of each message.

tldr.problem: Mail clients want to show a snippet of each message in the list, but generating it on the client requires multiple round trips and often downloads too much data.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8970 adds a PREVIEW FETCH item to IMAP. Servers that support the PREVIEW capability return a short UTF-8 text preview. An optional LAZY modifier lets servers return NIL if generating the preview would take too long.
tldr.outcome: Clients get consistent previews efficiently. RFC 8970 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2020 with no later obsoletions or updates.

today: RFC 8970 is a Proposed Standard published December 2020. It has not been obsoleted or updated; IANA added PREVIEW to the IMAP Capabilities registry.

sections.title: Why Servers Should Generate Previews
sections.content:
Many email clients show a small extract of message body text in the message list. RFC 8970 adds a PREVIEW extension to IMAP (RFC 3501), with servers advertising the PREVIEW capability.

Generating previews on the server gives consistent previews across all clients, saves bandwidth and round trips (client-side approaches often need FETCH BODYSTRUCTURE then FETCH BODY, and can't easily predict how much to fetch), and lets servers cache previews for the lifetime of a message.
sections.plainLanguage: If the server makes the summary, every client sees the same thing and doesn't have to open the whole message to make one.

sections.title: The PREVIEW FETCH Item
sections.content:
A client requests a preview by adding PREVIEW to a FETCH command (e.g. FETCH 1 (PREVIEW)). The server returns the preview as a variable-length string.

The server should try to return the same string each time, though clients must not assume it never changes. If the server cannot produce a meaningful preview (e.g. for encrypted messages or unsupported content types), it MUST return a zero-length string; clients SHOULD NOT ask again for that message.
sections.plainLanguage: You ask for a preview and get back a short string. If there's nothing useful to show, you get an empty string and shouldn't keep asking.

sections.title: Format and Length
sections.content:
The preview is treated as text/plain data, MUST be encoded in UTF-8, and MUST NOT be content transfer encoded. Servers should strip formatting markup to produce plain text.

Length is counted in preview characters (UCS characters encoded in UTF-8). Servers SHOULD limit to 200 preview characters and MUST NOT exceed 256. If the preview isn't based on the message body and the server supports LANGUAGE, descriptive text should follow language rules.
sections.plainLanguage: The preview is plain text in UTF-8, kept short - ideally 200 characters, never more than 256.

sections.title: The LAZY Modifier
sections.content:
The (LAZY) modifier after PREVIEW tells the server to return a preview only if it can do so without undue delay; otherwise it MUST return NIL. Every server supporting PREVIEW MUST implement LAZY. Servers MUST NOT return NIL when LAZY is not used.

Clients typically include PREVIEW (LAZY) when building the mailbox listing to avoid delays. Messages that return NIL are then fetched without LAZY in the background, ideally in batches (e.g. 50 messages). Clients SHOULD NOT repeatedly retry LAZY requests on a selected mailbox.
sections.plainLanguage: Lazy means 'only give me a preview if it's quick'. If it's slow, say 'not now' so I can show the rest of my list first.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content: Example 2 shows the lazy strategy: the client fetches messages 1-4 with ENVELOPE PREVIEW (LAZY). The server returns text for message 1, empty string for message 2, and NIL for messages 3 and 4. The client then fetches PREVIEW (without LAZY) for messages 3-4. Examples also show checking CAPABILITY for PREVIEW and combining with SEARCHRES to save round trips.
sections.plainLanguage: The client asks for previews if they're quick. It gets two right away, gets told 'not now' for the other two, then comes back for those two later.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Generating previews costs resources; servers should log client authentication identity for FETCH PREVIEW operations and may limit resource usage. In extreme cases this could result in empty previews.

Previews may contain sensitive data and must be protected with the same authorization and confidentiality controls as the source messages. If previews are cached, those protections must apply to the cached data too.
sections.plainLanguage: Summaries can be just as sensitive as the messages themselves, so they need the same protection. Servers also need to guard against someone overloading them with preview requests.
